title: Decay-window eviction and fragmentation telemetry sketch
content:
Summary:

Short proposal for a lightweight, windowed time-decay eviction policy combined with fragmentation-aware allocation hints and a small set of telemetry signals to drive compacting sweeps. Intended as a pragmatic, low-risk follow-up to our previous slab and pool experiments. Emphasis: predictable tail latency, fast hot-path (O(1) admission/hinting), and an incremental background compacting path that avoids global stop-the-world compaction.

Goals:
- Keep the admission/lookup/eviction hot path extremely cheap (few atomic ops).
- Reduce long-term memory fragmentation that causes token regen stalls and OOM spikes.
- Provide telemetry to answer: how much addressable free slack exists; what fraction of free is small fragments vs contiguous holes; tenant-level fragmentation debt.
- Allow graceful tenant-scoped reclamation (soft-evict tokens) before heavy compaction.

Non-goals:
- Replace fully-featured compactors in one release. This is an incremental design to reduce operator pain and guide a later compaction engine.

High-level idea:
1) Allocation layout: keep existing lane/slot model but add a tiny per-slot metadata word (16b) in front of each allocation that records: allocation_size_class, alloc_timestamp_bucket_id, and a 6-bit owner/tenant-id-hash. This is a constrained change to slot headers to avoid large perf regressions.
2) Hotness windows: instead of single-score LRU, we maintain a compact per-tenant decay-window histogram: N time buckets (e.g., 6 buckets representing [0-100ms,100-1s,1-10s,10-60s,1-10m,10m+]). Each request touch increments the bucket counter for that slot atomically (saturating small ints).
3) Admission and eviction policy: new entries are admitted to base lane; eviction prefers slots in highest-age/low-hotness buckets, but before ejecting a slot we consult a fragmentation heuristic (see below). In practice, eviction picks a candidate list from oldest buckets and scores by size_class_weight * frag_penalty * (1 + tenant_priority_weight).
4) Frag-aware allocation hinting: when tenant allocations frequently fail due to fragmentation (free_total >= requested && no contiguous block large enough), we emit a fragmentation event and mark that tenant as "fragged". For fragged tenants, we allow preemptive consolidation: small cold slots (age bucket >= 3) are eligible for cooperative micro-compaction (copy-out and free) during low load.
5) Background micro-compactor: runs per-shard, rate-limited, and operates on small contiguous regions (4KB-256KB). Each pass uses a fast scan of free-run-lengths and uses a cooperative copy protocol to move live slots to new packed regions, updating slot headers and KV index atomically via CAS. Avoids global locks by doing per-region CAS and a short-lived forwarding flag in moved slots.

Allocation and metadata details:
- Size classes: keep existing powers-of-two classes for <=64KB, but add an explicit medium class (3-16KB) with finer granularity to reduce internal fragmentation for typical tensor kv items.
- Per-slot header (16 bytes): 1 byte size_class, 1 byte age_bucket, 1 byte tenant_hash, 1 byte flags, 8 byte sequence/seqid (monotonic per-allocator page), 4 bytes reserved for checksum/validation. We will pack to 16 bytes.
- Free-run index: maintain a compact per-shard free-run RLE table stored in a ring buffer. Writers update with CAS; readers snapshot for the compactor. This avoids walking the whole heap.

Eviction scoring (pseudocode):
- candidate_slots = sample_from_bucket(oldest_bucket, k=32)
- score(s) = base_age_score(s.age_bucket) * size_penalty(size_class) * (1 + frag_penalty_for_tenant(s.tenant))
- select lowest scoring entries until reclaimed >= requested_size
- if candidate empties and reclaimed < requested, trigger micro-compact eligibility scan for that shard

Fragmentation telemetry (signals to surface in Console):
- free_contiguous_ratio: largest_free_block / total_free_bytes (per-shard, per-tenant)
- small_fragment_fraction: bytes_in_runs <= 4KB / total_free_bytes
- tenant_fragment_debt: estimate of additional bytes needed to service active allocation tails if compaction not done
- compaction_opportunity_index: heuristic combining frequency of allocation failures with free_contiguous_ratio
- slot_churn_rate: allocations+frees per-second per-tenant (helps decide if compaction will help)

Operator controls and autopilot hooks:
- soft_eviction_tokens: per-tenant counter earned by the autopilot (or support) that allows N soft evictions per-minute above normal quota; used to reclaim slack without compaction
- compaction_budget: global BG compaction rate (MB/s) and per-shard floor/ceiling
- eager_consolidation_mode: boolean toggle to be used temporarily for on-call interventions

Safety and correctness notes:
- Forwarding flag: when micro-compactor moves an object, it marks old slot with a forward pointer and CAS-updates the KV index to point to the new slot. Readers that see the forwarding flag must follow it. This is similar to our prior relocation sketches but with a smaller, per-region scope.
- Crash consistency: compactor writes are durable in new slot before flipping index; on restart, a short recovery pass reclaims half-completed moves by scanning forward flags and finishing them or rolling back. Recovery cost bounded by compaction window and small region size.

Performance expectations (back-of-envelope):
- Hot-path hit latency: unchanged within noise (<5% regression) since header reads are small and bucket increment is a single fetch-add on a compact counter.
- Background compaction overhead: configurable; target <= 5% CPU at steady-state for mid-size clusters when compaction_budget=medium.
- Expected reduction in allocation failures due to fragmentation: 40-70% in workloads we observed in benchmarks where allocs are medium-sized (2-12KB) and churn high.

Experiments and measurements to run (next sprint):
1) Microbench harness: synthetic tenant with 60% medium-size items, churn 100k ops/s on a shard; compare baseline vs histogram-decay admission and micro-compaction. Measure tail p50/p95/p99 for alloc and token-gen latency.
2) Telemetry validation: inject controlled fragmentation cases (lots of alternating frees/allocs of sizes 2KB and 8KB) and measure free_contiguous_ratio and small_fragment_fraction correlation with allocation failures.
3) Failure and recovery: force process kill during compaction pass to validate bounded recovery cost.
4) Tenant soft-eviction UX: simulate autopilot giving tokens and measure application-level error surface.

Open questions / risks:
- Header size vs performance: can we keep header <=12 bytes? 16 is safer but increases metadata bandwidth. Benchmarks required.
- Tenant_hash collisions: we use small tenant_hash to keep header small. How often will collisions cause incorrect frag accounting? Probably acceptable but needs simulation.
- Backpressure interactions: if compaction lags behind allocation failures, we may oscillate. We need hysteresis in autopilot token issuance.
- Cold-copy amplification: moving items can double write amplification. Must keep budget low and prefer copying very cold slots.

Rollout plan (phased):
A) Canary: add header and decay-window histogram hooks, disable compactor. Run in canary for 2 weeks to validate hot-path perf.
B) Telemetry: enable signals to Console and compute compaction_opportunity_index for a few customers; alert when tenant_fragment_debt > threshold.
C) Soft-evict tokens: expose autopilot knob and validate UX with ops team.
D) Micro-compactor opt-in: enable compactor at low-budget on dedicated test shards, iterate.
E) Full rollout with adaptive budget and default-on for new clusters.

Implementation notes / PRs to open:
- allocator: add per-slot header packing, new size class, and histogram buckets (PR: serving-runtime#3412)
- compactor: new micro-compactor module with per-shard rate limiter and forwarding protocol
- observability: Console metrics and per-tenant telemetry export (short-lived experiments)

TODOs:
- [ ] run header-size microbenchmark (Ravi)
- [ ] implement free-run RLE snapshot (Jonas)
- [ ] simulation of tenant_hash collision rates (Elena)
- [ ] draft Console panel mockups (Samir)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on the compaction side; primary value is better telemetry and smarter eviction so we reduce operational pain without a heavy compactor rollout.
- I'm particularly interested in feedback on header packing trade-offs and compaction budget semantics.
